clue.text: Do the French provide a job seeker's allowance?

parts.note: taken as written
le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A question about whether French people pay unemployment benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: THE DOLE is everyday British slang for unemployment benefit, paid to people looking for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dole is the informal British name for state unemployment benefit, money given to someone out of work.

clue.text: Received letters from him, although he was unfaithful.

indicators.note: the letters of the clue word are taken from it and set down in a new order

explanation.surface: A betrayed partner reads letters from a lover who had been cheating all along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters from' tells you to take the letters of RECEIVED and rearrange them; the definition names the kind of man who cheats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who was unfaithful misled a partner, so is a cheat or betrayer.

clue.text: … and a letter about your first door frame

indicators.note: the letter's word goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: an epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of 'your' is used

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a letter and a door frame somehow belong together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts Y, the first letter of 'your', inside EPISTLE. The leading dots and 'and' just join this clue to the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistyle is the architrave, the beam laid across columns, which also names the moulded frame round a doorway.

clue.text: One who comes out against an examination for a worker

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a test is an examination
the worker ant is a crossword staple for a worker

explanation.surface: Someone who emerges to protest against a test set for an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' here means enters the arena to compete, not emerges in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor steps out onto the field or stage to take part, so is one who comes out.

clue.text: Angry about having to go to the other side…

parts.note: cross means angry
over can mean about, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at being made to move across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a road or border is to pass from one side to the far one.

clue.text: … in spite of being able to sit down

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: despite being able to take a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as NOT WITH STANDING: not on your feet, so seated.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding means despite; read in pieces it also describes someone who is not upright, i.e. seated.

clue.text: The surprise opening against the French

indicators.note: against means set right beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a start is an opening or beginning
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: An unexpected first move made against French opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: A tin so placed to hold a prickly plant

parts.note: a can is a tin
thus means so, in that manner

explanation.surface: A tin positioned to contain a spiny plant, like a makeshift pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed to hold' says the three pieces, set side by side, make up the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Purport to be a singer

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to be a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist or purport of a document is its general drift; a high male voice in a choir is also so named.

clue.text: Place to make a bad mistake in company

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside company's letters

parts.note: a sin is a grave wrong, a bad mistake

explanation.surface: Where one might go to commit a serious error while out with others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at gambling away money, which is apt for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a venue for gambling, a place where bets are made.

clue.text: Attempt to get more the second time around

definitions.text: Attempt to get more the second time around

parts.words: Attempt to get more the second time around
parts.note: describes having one more go at something after a first failure, as a lottery ticket might urge

explanation.surface: Trying for a bigger haul on a second go.
explanation.definitionFit: Making another effort after failing means having a second shot at the same thing.

clue.text: Seeing a problem for one I stir up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: up, after stir, signals the letters are mixed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices a difficulty for a friend and makes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir up' reads as one phrase meaning cause trouble, but only 'up' signals the rearrangement; 'stir' supplies letters. 'Seeing a problem' means a problem with seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the iris, an eye condition that troubles vision.

clue.text: I'm taking two articles to a first rate copier

annotationWithheld.why: I'm taking two articles to a first rate copier (8) IMITATOR: I'M ... TO + R leaves ITA, which 'two articles' cannot honestly give; no source found for the setter's parse
annotationWithheld.clue: I'm taking two articles to a first rate copier

clue.text: Sort of relationship which could be on or off

definitions.text: Sort of relationship which could be on or off

parts.words: Sort of relationship which could be on or off
parts.note: a stormy bond that swings between fondness and loathing, on one moment and off the next

explanation.surface: A partnership that keeps flickering between together and apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A relationship mixing strong affection with strong dislike flips between warm and cold.

clue.text: The pieces cut off — or put on!

explanation.surface: Scraps removed from something, or decorations added to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clippings shorn away when tidying are one sense; garnishes or extras added, as with a roast dinner, are the other.

clue.text: This plant came up!

explanation.surface: A plant that has sprouted.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub with thorny stems is one sense; the past tense of ascend or get up is the other.

clue.text: Roll out some sort of steel shoe-not the left one

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the words are knocked into a fresh order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Unrolling a type of steel to make armour footwear, but not for the left foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some sort of' is a second hint to rearrange; 'not the left one' means the pool keeps only two of its three Ls, since L stands for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A solleret is the jointed metal foot covering of a suit of armour.

clue.text: Go slow in the centre of this city

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the two words, with one letter left on each side

explanation.surface: Advice to drive slowly downtown.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: Musician gets another roasting

indicators.note: another signals a different arrangement of the word's letters

explanation.surface: A performer gets another dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasting' looks like a severe telling-off; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays the church instrument with pipes is a musician.

clue.text: Has fixed ideas, the boss sees difficulties

indicators.note: difficulties suggests the letters are in trouble and must be sorted out

explanation.surface: The manager spots problems and becomes fixated.
explanation.definitionFit: One who is preoccupied keeps returning to the same thought, as fixed ideas take hold.

clue.text: To be more beautiful was of less importance about last December

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: petty means trivial, so pettier means of less importance

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of 'December' is used

explanation.surface: Being more attractive used to matter less around the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, the last letter of 'December', inside PETTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Prettier is the comparative of pretty, meaning lovelier or more attractive.

clue.text: About a thousand in support, that's first class

indicators.note: in means these letters go into the support's word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Roughly a thousand backing something that is top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means foremost or best, as in the Premier League.

clue.text: Put a pigeon in an old cannon

parts.note: culver is an old word for a pigeon or dove
taken as written

explanation.surface: Loading a bird into an antique gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A culverin was a long-barrelled cannon of the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: This priest is a hundred soon!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A clergyman about to reach his centenary.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Roughly agree with first man that's not much

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of 'man' and puts it at the front
roughly means the letters of the word are only approximately in order

explanation.surface: Grudgingly going along with the first fellow when there is little to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' turns AGREE into EAGRE; 'first man' gives M, placed at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty, a small and inadequate amount.

clue.text: An awful crisis causes bloomers to be made

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: A dreadful emergency leads to embarrassing blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like mistakes or underwear; it means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are spring flowers such as daffodils, so they are things that bloom.

clue.text: Horses sound as though they're refusing

indicators.note: as though signals the cry is heard like another word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: nays are votes or answers of no, so people refusing say nays

explanation.surface: The noise horses make seems like a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses whinny, which is their call or cry.

clue.text: Normal gossip, coming from offshore?

parts.note: natural means normal or to be expected
gas is idle chatter, gossip

explanation.surface: Ordinary chit-chat arriving from out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the fuel by where it is drilled, such as North Sea rigs; the question mark flags the indirect description.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane fuel is extracted from rigs drilled into the seabed, so it is produced out at sea.

clue.text: Square works best

parts.note: T stands for a square, as in the T-square used by draughtsmen
ops is short for opera, the plural of opus, meaning works

explanation.surface: A town square functioning at its finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' is a verb here: to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or outdo someone is to come out on top of them.
